stories.headline: Anthropic Finalizes $1.5B Joint Venture With Blackstone, Goldman Sachs to Sell AI to PE Portfolios

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is finalizing an approximately $1.5 billion joint venture with Blackstone, Goldman Sachs, Hellman & Friedman, and General Atlantic to sell AI tools to private-equity-backed companies.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic was finalising an approximately $1.5bn joint venture with a small group of Wall Street firms, with an announcement expected as soon as Monday.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic, Blackstone, and Hellman & Friedman are each expected to invest roughly $300 million; Goldman Sachs is set to invest around $150 million as a founding investor.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic, Blackstone and Hellman & Friedman are anchoring the deal, and each company is expected to invest roughly $300 million... Goldman Sachs is also set to be a founding investor, putting in around $150 million.

key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI announced a similar joint venture, DeployCo, last month, anchored by TPG, Bain Capital, Advent International, Brookfield, and Goanna Capital. The five PE firms together committed about $4bn.

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Security Public Beta for Enterprise Vulnerability Scanning

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced the public beta of Claude Security, a cybersecurity tool that scans codebases, detects vulnerabilities, and generates patches, powered by Claude Opus 4.7.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has announced the public beta for Claude Security, its cybersecurity tool used for scanning codebases, detecting vulnerabilities, and generating patches.

key_facts.fact: Claude Security can scan full enterprise repositories and open Claude Code to fix vulnerabilities in a single session, with one-click scanning that analyzes component relationships and data usage.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Security can scan full enterprise repositories to flag potential flaws – then open Claude Code to fix them – to reduce detection and response to one session for cyber workers.

key_facts.fact: The tool attaches a confidence percentage to each finding to reduce false positives, and now includes scheduled and targeted scans plus export to Slack, Jira, CSV, and Markdown.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic tweaked the tool to place a greater emphasis on validating AI findings, attaching a confidence percentage to each finding to reduce false positives. New additions also include scheduled and targeted scans, as well as the option to export findings to Slack, Jira, or as CSV and Markdown files.

key_facts.fact: Claude Security was previously known as Claude Code Security, first made available to select organizations as a research preview; it is now accessible within Claude or via a dedicated website page.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Security was previously known as Claude Code Security, which Anthropic first made available to select organizations as a research preview... Claude Security is accessible directly within Claude, or via a dedicated page on its website.

key_facts.fact: The launch follows the UK AI Security Institute's independent verification that Anthropic's Mythos Preview was the first model to complete a 32-step enterprise network attack simulation.
key_facts.excerpt: The UK's AI Security Institute (AISI) has independently verified that the model is more capable at cyber tasks, and that it was the first to complete a 32-step enterprise network attack simulation designed to test LLM cyber exploit capabilities.

stories.headline: EU's €20B AI Gigafactory Plan Faces Criticism Over Demand Doubts and Nvidia GPU Dependency

key_facts.fact: European Commission plans €20 billion for 4-5 AI gigafactories with 100,000+ GPUs each, forming Europe's answer to OpenAI's $500B Stargate project
key_facts.excerpt: Commission President Ursula von der Leyen outlined the ambition in February last year, proposing four to five mega computing facilities, each powered by 100,000 GPUs, forming Europe's answer to OpenAI's 500 billion dollar Stargate project.

key_facts.fact: 76 bids for 60 sites across 16 countries were filed, but legislators and experts question whether actual demand exists for the compute capacity
key_facts.excerpt: A total of 76 bids for 60 sites across 16 countries were filed during an informal sense-check last year. But legislators and experts say which companies would use this computing power remains unclear.

key_facts.fact: A group of 18 European Parliament lawmakers warned the Commission about dependency on Nvidia as a single chip supplier, questioning how the plan reduces strategic dependencies
key_facts.excerpt: A group of 18 European Parliament lawmakers warned the Commission about dependency on a single chip supplier, questioning how the gigafactory initiative would reduce Europe's strategic dependencies.

key_facts.fact: Mistral is not waiting for gigafactories: announced $1.2B data center in Sweden in February and raised hundreds of millions for a Paris facility in March
key_facts.excerpt: Europe's most prominent AI developer, Mistral, isn't waiting for the gigafactories. In February, it announced a 1.2 billion dollar data center investment in Sweden. At the end of March, it raised hundreds of millions of euros for a facility near Paris.

key_facts.fact: Commission defended plan as about 'sovereign compute' with data 'fully protected under European law, without the possibility of third country interference'
key_facts.excerpt: The Commission's spokesperson Thomas Regnier pushed back. 'This is not just about raw compute power, it's about sovereign compute,' he said.

key_facts.fact: Siemens warned EU regulations are pushing its AI spending outside Europe; financing model requires 65% from private parties, already causing delays
key_facts.excerpt: Siemens recently warned that EU regulations are pushing its AI spending outside Europe… the gigafactory financing model requires 65 percent from private parties, and that structure is already causing delays in some member states.

stories.headline: Five Eyes Intelligence Alliance Publishes Joint Guidance Warning Against Rapid Agentic AI Adoption

key_facts.fact: CISA, NSA, and cybersecurity agencies from the UK, Australia, Canada, and New Zealand co-authored guidance titled 'Careful adoption of agentic AI services' published on Friday May 2.
key_facts.excerpt: The agencies delivered that position last Friday in a guide titled Careful adoption of agentic AI services [PDF]

key_facts.fact: The document lists 23 different risks and over 100 individual best practices, warning that every component in an agentic AI system widens the attack surface.
key_facts.excerpt: The document contains more scary stories, then lists 23 different risks and over 100 individual best practices to address them.

key_facts.fact: The agencies warn organizations should 'assume that agentic AI systems may behave unexpectedly' and prioritize 'resilience, reversibility and risk containment over efficiency gains.'
key_facts.excerpt: Until security practices, evaluation methods and standards mature, organisations should assume that agentic AI systems may behave unexpectedly and plan deployments accordingly, prioritizing resilience, reversibility and risk containment over efficiency gains.

key_facts.fact: The guidance recommends organizations should 'never grant broad or unrestricted access, especially to sensitive data' and 'only use agentic AI for low-risk and non-sensitive tasks.'
key_facts.excerpt: Safely using AI agents means 'never granting it broad or unrestricted access, especially to sensitive data or critical systems,' the document warns. Companies, it says, 'should only use agentic AI for low-risk and non-sensitive tasks.'

key_facts.fact: The agencies note that threat intelligence for agentic AI is still evolving, with OWASP and MITRE ATLAS currently focused on LLMs, leaving some attack vectors unique to agentic AI unaddressed.
key_facts.excerpt: Threat intelligence for agentic AI systems is still evolving... resources like the Open Web Application Security Project and MITRE ATLAS currently focus on LLMs. As a result, some attack vectors unique to agentic AI may not be fully captured or addressed.

sources.title: Five Eyes spook shops warn rapid rollouts of agentic AI are too risky

stories.headline: GameStop Makes Unsolicited ~$56B Offer to Buy eBay, Cohen Ready to Go Hostile

key_facts.fact: GameStop proposed on Sunday to buy eBay for ~$56B at $125/share in a 50-50 cash-and-stock deal, a 20% premium to eBay's Friday close
key_facts.excerpt: GameStop proposed on Sunday to buy eBay Inc for about $56 billion in a cash-and-stock deal. GameStop is offering to pay $125 a share in a 50-50 mix of cash and stock. Based on eBay's Friday close, the bid represents a premium of about 20%.

key_facts.fact: GameStop has built a ~5% stake in eBay and secured a $20B commitment letter from TD Bank for debt financing
key_facts.excerpt: Cohen said he has already lined up financial commitments, including a commitment letter for about $20 billion in debt from TD Securities. The U.S. videogame retailer has already built up a 5% stake in eBay.

key_facts.fact: GameStop had ~$9.4B in cash as of January 31; the company's market cap was ~$12B vs eBay's ~$46B, making it a dramatic reverse-scale acquisition
key_facts.excerpt: GameStop had about $9.4 billion in cash and liquid investments as of January 31. GameStop had a market value of nearly $12 billion at the close of business on Friday, while eBay had a market value of about $46 billion.

key_facts.fact: Cohen said he would pursue a proxy fight if eBay's board is unreceptive, and aims to cut $2B of eBay's annualized costs within 12 months
key_facts.excerpt: Cohen said in the letter that GameStop would cut $2 billion of eBay's annualized costs within 12 months of close. He told the Wall Street Journal he was prepared to pursue a proxy fight.

key_facts.fact: Cohen told WSJ he wants to make eBay 'a legit competitor to Amazon' and is 'thinking about turning eBay into something worth hundreds of billions of dollars'
key_facts.excerpt: 'It could be a legit competitor to Amazon,' Cohen said about eBay. 'I'm thinking about turning eBay into something worth hundreds of billions of dollars.'

key_facts.excerpt: June output quotas will stand at 9.762 mln bpd for Russia, at 10.291 mln bpd for Saudi Arabia, at 4.352 mln bpd for Iraq, at 2.628 mln bpd for Kuwait.

key_facts.fact: The increase aims to accelerate compensation for overproduction since January 2024, following the UAE's withdrawal from OPEC+
key_facts.excerpt: This measure will provide an opportunity for the participating countries to accelerate their compensation. They also confirmed their intention to fully compensate for any overproduced volume since January 2024.

key_facts.fact: US national average gas price hit $4.45/gallon, up from $2.98 before the Iran war began, after surging ~30 cents in the prior week
key_facts.excerpt: The national average price for a gallon of gas was $4.45 as of Sunday, according to AAA. That's up from $2.98 right before the war in Iran began, with AAA reporting a few days ago that gas prices shot up nearly 30 cents in the previous week.

key_facts.fact: US Treasury Secretary Bessent said oil prices could start declining within 3 to 9 months, citing the UAE's OPEC exit and oil tankers stranded in the Gulf
key_facts.excerpt: The UAE has decided that OPEC is not for them. Most monopolies eventually collapse under their own weight. This gives me a lot of optimism that oil prices on the other side of this conflict are going to be much lower.

stories.headline: Trump Launches 'Project Freedom' to Escort Ships From Strait of Hormuz as Iran Sends 14-Point Plan

key_facts.fact: Trump announced 'Project Freedom' starting Monday to help stranded ships leave the Strait of Hormuz, calling it a humanitarian gesture for 'neutral and innocent' countries
key_facts.excerpt: Trump said 'Project Freedom' would begin Monday morning in the Middle East. Trump added that his representatives are having discussions with Iran that could lead to something 'very positive for all.'

key_facts.fact: Iran sent a 14-point counterproposal via Pakistan calling for nonaggression guarantees, sanctions relief, lifting the naval blockade, and ending the war 'on all fronts' including Lebanon
key_facts.excerpt: Tehran has sent a 14-point plan to Washington, calling for guarantees of nonaggression, sanctions relief, the lifting of a naval blockade and an end to the war 'on all fronts', including in Lebanon.

key_facts.fact: Trump expressed doubt the proposal would be acceptable, saying Iran 'has not yet paid a big enough price for what they have done to humanity, and the world, over the last 47 years'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump on Saturday said he was reviewing the proposal but expressed doubt it would lead to a deal, saying on social media that 'they have not yet paid a big enough price for what they have done to Humanity, and the World, over the last 47 years.'

key_facts.fact: The IRGC said it is on standby for a return to war, saying a resumption of hostilities is 'likely' as evidence shows the US 'is not committed to any agreements or treaties'
key_facts.excerpt: The IRGC said it is on standby for a return to war with the US, saying a resumption of hostilities is 'likely' as 'evidence shows that [the US] is not committed to any agreements or treaties'.

key_facts.excerpt: Al Jazeera reported that Iran offered to 'discuss the idea' of pausing uranium enrichment for 'up to 15 years,' which is longer than previous Iranian proposals to pause enrichment for up to five years.

stories.headline: Neuralink Unveils Next-Generation Surgical Robot for Brain Implant Insertion

key_facts.fact: Neuralink published a video showcasing the next generation of its surgical robot designed to automate insertion of flexible electrode threads into the brain for the Neuralink implant.
key_facts.excerpt: We've built a surgical robot to automate key steps in the process of receiving a Neuralink implant to promote safety, reliability, and scalability.

key_facts.fact: The robot uses eight cameras, an OCT (optical coherence tomography) sensor that can see through the surface of the brain, and five axes of movement to reach all regions of the brain.
key_facts.excerpt: There's a OCT system which stands for optical coherence tomography. This sensor allows us to see through the surface. So this robot has to move in five axes to reach all the regions of the brain.

key_facts.fact: The threads are too fine for a surgeon to place by hand; Neuralink engineers compare the task to placing single strands of hair into jello, hundreds of times.
key_facts.excerpt: Imagine placing a single strand of hair into jello, and then having to do that hundreds of times.

key_facts.fact: Neuralink's stated goal is to streamline the procedure to be comparable to Lasik eye surgery in order to scale brain implants to thousands or millions of people.
key_facts.excerpt: We have to think from first principles, how to solve each step and how to combine them together to provide an amazing experience that compares to Lasik surgery.

sources.title: Automating Neurosurgery with Robotics | Neuralink
